messages:
kiran: quick follow-up from the admission API brainstorm. we still need a concrete contract for telling the scheduler how urgent a request is without leaking a huge abuse vector. ideas?
liz: we've discussed score vs hard priority. another axis is "suppressible priority" — a higher priority that the scheduler can revoke if abuse signals spike.
sam: define revoke rules? we don't want customer-facing flakiness.
kiran: sketch: admission can return priority_kind: [soft, suppressible, guaranteed]. soft=score float. suppressible includes a nonce + budget weight. guaranteed = hard priority with strict auditing + manual approval only for enterprise.
maya: sounds workable. how would scheduler treat suppressible? e.g., temporarily elevate queue position but with TTL and a local kill-switch if anomalies seen.
liz: exactly. implementation notes: suppressible gets a nonce that increments a per-tenant counter; scheduler tracks per-tenant live-elevations and a global suppression budget. if budget drained or anomaly detected (spike shape mismatch, token reuse), scheduler drops elevations and emits events.
sam: where to place abuse checks? pre-issuance at admission or post-acceptance monitoring? both?
kiran: both. admission rejects obvious patterns (burst-of-nonces, entropy failures). scheduler does runtime checks (latency drift, sudden error rate) and revokes. security/abuse owns the ML model that flags issuance.
maya: metrics: per-tenant suppressible_issued, suppressible_accepted, suppressible_revoked, suppressible_reject_reasons. plus global suppressible_budget, budget_decay_rate. ops-bot: (automated) created ticket: infra-ops/PRIORITY-SUPPRESSIBLE-METRICS-1
liz: protobuf change proposal: TokenReply { string token = 1; int32 ttl_s = 2; float soft_score = 3; oneof priority { SuppressiblePriority suppressible = 10; GuaranteedPriority guaranteed = 11; } } SuppressiblePriority { string nonce = 1; int32 weight = 2; int64 expiry_ms = 3; }
sam: audit trail: nonce issuance must be logged with tenant, request pattern snapshot, and a signature so we can trace back misuse. plus retention 90 days.
kiran: tradeoffs summary: A) soft-only: least risk, worst SLO guarantees. B) guaranteed-only: simplest scheduling, highest abuse & ops burden. C) hybrid w/ suppressible: balances both but needs more infra & ops telemetry. leaning C but want strong safeties.
maya: testing plan: unit tests for nonce lifecycle, integration tests for budget decay, canary where suppressible is honored only for internal tenants first. run adversarial suite: many small fast requests, nonce replay attempts, nonce theft simulation.
liz: rollout steps: 1) proto + audit schema PR, 2) admission starts issuing suppressible nonces behind flag (scheduler ignores them), 3) telemetry + dashboards in place, 4) enable scheduler honoring nonces in canary, 72h watch, 5) staged enable for paid tiers.
sam: alerts: create low-noise alerts keyed to revocation rate/nonce-failure-rate so oncall sees signal before customer impact. add automatic rollback if revocation rate > X in Y minutes.
ops-bot: (deploy) branch created: feat/suppressible-priority. CI started.
kiran: action items: @liz handle proto + audit retention doc, @maya metrics + test harness, @sam alerts + runbook, I'll own admission + scheduler glue. reconvene in 48h for PR sync.
liz: will draft proto now and send for quick review.
maya: I'll schedule canary windows and start creating synthetic attack scenarios.
sam: I'll draft runbook and pre-populate dashboards.
kiran: thanks all — want RFC follow-up with concrete thresholds next week.
